content: The sclera is the dense, opaque, and typically white outer layer of the eye. It is composed of fibrous tissue containing collagen and elastic fibers, which contribute to its strength and flexibility. In children, the sclera is thinner, allowing some of the underlying pigmentation to show through, giving it a slightly bluish appearance. In older individuals, fatty deposits can accumulate on the sclera, causing it to appear slightly yellow. The sclera constitutes the posterior five-sixths of the connective tissue layer that encases the eyeball. It plays a critical role in maintaining the structural integrity and shape of the globe, resisting both internal and external forces. Additionally, it serves as the site of attachment for the extraocular muscles, which are responsible for eye movement.
